steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph. I'm starting to regret this.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Sneaking in here... was not a good idea.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The higher the place, the more complete and larger the shadows are.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But this place is a little too high up...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: ...Can you let me go?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No can do, girlie.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Don't you get any funny ideas either.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This ship is way too big. I'd really appreciate a cute girl helping me keep an eye out for any soldiers popping up.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Do you also call yourself a Victorian Sarkaz?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No, I'm a Kazdel Sarkaz.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Wait, but... if you're a Kazdel Sarkaz...? Then why are you...?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Aren't you working for General Manfred and the Military Commission?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I work only for myself.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Where's this ship headed?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I don't like seeing kids suffer.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I... I don't know...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I really don't!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What exactly is your job here?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Um... being a Sarkaz mercenary?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Heh. A Sarkaz mercenary who hasn't killed before.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You can't even silently draw your weapon while being captured.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What's Manfred even planning to do here? Open a kindergarten?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: General Manfred says he wants me to learn what war is.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Well, how's that going?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I think it's just people killing another group of people.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Congratulations, we share the same view.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This ship sure flies high.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: The General says it's because it's a revenant.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Ugh. A revenant. So that's why.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's why Ascalon was in so much pain. Good thing they're conspicuous.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This ship is still ascending.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Judging by our heading... it's not flying towards the battlefield. This ship is returning to Londinium.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You flew out of Londinium, fired a shot at the Duke's warship, and then stopped for a few days in Norport Borough.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And now that the dukes are on their way with their fleets, you're retreating?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Seems like I need to change my impression of Manfred. Not only is he passionate about pedagogy, but he likes to take the ship out for little drives too?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Alright, you don't know anything at all.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Paprika.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: So you're the Paprika mentioned in the report I read. You freed the workers from Munitions Factory No. 11, and then you were caught by Manfred.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: For a Sarkaz mercenary, is that... not honorable?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: For a Sarkaz mercenary, honor is the worst kind of shame.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You've been to Kazdel before, right? What is it like?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: My old captain told me that it's our homeland.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Where did you grow up?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Columbia.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No wonder.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Every Sarkaz that hasn't been to Kazdel thinks it's probably an adorable, sweet little place.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: That's just your own wishful thinking.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Think of the filthiest, most disgusting, any derogatory adjective you can muster, and multiply that by a hundred—now that's Kazdel.

spans.text: Think of the filthiest, most disgusting, any derogatory adjective you can muster, and multiply that by a hundred—now

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Sounds like most people wouldn't like it.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Then why... why do so many Sarkaz call it home?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Because they need a home.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: They think, as long as they have a home, everything will fall neatly into place, all discrimination and persecution against them will cease and they'll once again be able to puff out their chests in pride.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmph. It's silly.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Or maybe you think that... because you're not a Sarkaz?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You like to ask questions, little girl, but that's not a good habit in wartime.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I... I was only making a guess! Please don't get angry!

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: ...I'm just real curious.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Nobody here wants to talk to me, and General Manfred is always busy.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: They're all so excited and always talk about doing great things... but why don't I feel it?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: All I've seen is familiar faces dying one by one, getting replaced by fresh faces, but when those become familiar...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: The same thing just happens again and again.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I feel like I shouldn't be here at all.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Does it actually matter if someone is really a Sarkaz or not?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If everyone thinks you're a Sarkaz, then you might as well grind down your horns and pretend to be one.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Because you can only survive as a Sarkaz.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And when it comes to surviving, your feelings don't matter at all.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: And that's why you joined this war with the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Seems like you should stay with Manfred a while longer. He hasn't taught you the most important things you need to know about war.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: General Manfred lent me a book, A History of Sarkaz War.

spans.text: General Manfred lent me a book,

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I know the author. His name is Hoederer, and he's an idiot.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: 'Sarkaz War,' 'Victorian War,' 'Ducal War,' 'Royal Court War,' only an idiot talks about stuff like that.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Who'd be arrogant enough to claim a war for themselves? I sure wouldn't, at least.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: War is war, and that's all there is to it.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You don't believe this war can save us all... Then what do you believe in?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I believe when you're hungry, you have to eat, when you're thirsty, you need to drink, swinging your arms around for too long will tire you out, and if I jump out of this ship I will die.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I only believe in these things that can't be given meaning.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Toying around with 'meaning' is the root of all suffering.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: In the same way, I believe that profits make people impulsive, fear makes them impatient, a burning fire can not be easily extinguished, and the resulting conflicts cannot be easily ended.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ines, as a guest, you should have greeted me first.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's been a while, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Indeed it has.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: So, why don't you stay? You can admire the scenery with us.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The storm is approaching quickly.
Ines and Manfred turn to look out the window.
They see the smoke and dust rising in the distance, and several high-speed battleship fleets approaching.
This airship high up in the sky is attracting the attention of every ducal force already stationed nearby.
A sudden flash of clarity shoots through Ines upon seeing these little battleships scrambling like insects in the shadow of the airship.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You want the flames.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No, the flames have already been ignited, you're just... using this ship as kindling to keep it in the air.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Caster, Wellington, Windermere, and maybe Normandy too...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The representatives of these greedy dukes are already all gathered on this plate, while their masters' fleets observe their rivals as they make their way here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This airship is moving so slowly because you're waiting for them, you're tempting them.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The dukes would rather not let the airship hide behind Londinium's robust city walls, so they'll gather here...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And this is what you've all been waiting for.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: An perfectly little... shooting gallery for The Shard.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Should I be glad that Hoederer's partner is so sharp?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: A shame you put it together so late.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Men, seize her.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: So what did she tell you, Paprika?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: She said, war is war, and that's all there is to it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Indeed, that's all.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If she could just see the big picture, just how many things surrounding war would she see?
This intelligence must be delivered.
Ines has to admit that the Military Commission has drawn up a brilliant plan.
She can foresee what will happen next.
The Shard's Catastrophe will severely damage the dukes' forces, and furthermore, said damage will be credited to not just the Sarkaz, but also to their respective rivals.
And once Victoria's storm-bringing prowess is drawn out into the open, any country across the lands will feel fear, and also fury.
Every seat of power will want to destroy this one, or possess it for themselves.
What if, at this time—the dukes guarding the borders slack on their duties because of their infighting?
Leithanien, Ursus, Kazimierz, and even the old Gaulish regions would never let this opportunity slip.
This is only the first flame.
Soon, an unstoppable blaze will sweep across the entire land.
Ines knows, there is still time, it's not too late.
As long as she can get the information out—
A shadow approaches at the end of the corridor. It is not her own shadow, but the owner of this vessel.
Ines, who has heard rumors from her old partner about the revenant, is for the first time in her life glad that she isn't a real Sarkaz.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Yep, shadow's still there.
The sun rises, the long night having finally passed, and the mobile plate below her casts an extremely long shadow.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Right.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I should thank myself for finding such a high place.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I'm guessing that a jump from here would probably kill me.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Heh, who would have thought that today, the Ines who always comes back from the brink of death, is finally embracing it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer and W are gonna laugh themselves to death.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I hope they don't get to see me in such a wretched state.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: —*exhale*
She falls, a gale blowing through her hair, and she can hardly keep her eyes open.
But it is only at this height that she can take all the shadows of Norport into her view.
Only at this height can she manipulate these shadows that stretch as far as she can see.
She knows that she only has a few seconds to make it, quickly falling into the shadows before her.
Now.
Death is already lingering beyond the door.
